 As UNDP advances its COVID-19 response in SIDS, we recognize the importance of safeguarding livelihoods as the foundation upon which economies and industries are rebuilt and strengthened. #SIDS leadership is demonstrating that an inclusive, collaborative, climate-smart response to COVID-19 is not only possible but that it is the way forward. 
In this issue, we highlight the importance of achieving food and livelihood security in SIDS, not just in our COVID-19 response, but in the development of more sustainable islands. SIDS are pioneering new tools and technologies for conservation, adaptation, recovery and response - championing the very values set forth by the #Paris Agreement, #SAMOA Pathway and the #SDGs. SIDS are certainly experiencing significant disruptions and losses in light of COVID-19, but through the use of data, technology and the collaborative partnerships, we're witnessing an agile, action-oriented response to their most pressing needs.
Very best regards,

What is the future of development?

The future is not what it used to be. A crisis can change the world from one day to the next, with tragic consequences.

But the actions countries take as they prepare, respond and recover in the face of the COVID-19 pandemic will lay the foundations for a fair and just transition to the future – a new social contract.

That is why, as the UN’s leading agency on development, UNDP is not working to help people “get back to normal”. Normal was not good enough.

With the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) as our compass, we want people to get back to something better – a future everyone believes in, where no one is left behind.

export-urn-li-share-6693605004244340737.caption:
To restore Cuba’s mangroves, the ‘Reduction of vulnerability to coastal flooding through ecosystem-based adaptation in the south of Artemisa and Mayabeque Provinces’ project focusses on an 84 kilometre stretch of coastline between Punta Sucia and Punta Mora on the southern coast.

The restoration includes comprehensive reforestation, increased monitoring and control, and detailed vulnerability assessments to better understand how climate change is affecting communities and their ecosystems.

Four years in, mangroves are sprouting, populations of wildlife, shrimp, and fish are increasing, and flooding is more controlled

Please find the UNDP SIDS Bulletin issue 19 here:
https://lnkd.in/gyyDkbG

As has been highlighted many times, the COVID-19 pandemic has laid bare the structural vulnerabilities #SIDS face. It is predicted that SIDS will experience contractions in GDP between 8 and 15 percent in 2020, recovery from the global crisis will take years and will be costly. With progress on the #2030agenda threatened, we are reminded of the need for a multidimensional vulnerability index to accurately reflect the special development case of SIDS in line with the goals of the #SAMOA Pathway. SIDS clearly express the urgent need to reexamine the eligibility criteria for enabling access to concessional finance or restructure debt in order to create fiscal space to finance recovery.

In this bulletin we explores inspiring youth climate engagement, seizing #digital opportunities and transforming #tourism. The stories and best practices shared in this bulletin remind us of the opportunities SIDS have for overcoming their challenges even in the midst of the current global health and development crisis. With strong commitment, ambition and durable partnerships, we can all rise up for SIDS to help them build forward better.

#RisingUpForSIDS #undp

As we continue to have more conversations surrounding #digital finance in SIDS, I would like to highlight an important piece from our 23rd Bulletin.

Many had predicted that the rate of remittances in SIDS would fall during the pandemic. They account for an average of 10% of GDP in Pacific #SIDS; so, it would’ve been a devastating loss. However, the pandemic appears to have led to an uptick in digitally enabled remittances.

• Money sent to Fiji via the M-PAiSA Mobile Money app, developed by Vodafone with the support of the Pacific Financial Inclusion Programme (PFIP), quadrupled between February and August.
• ANZ Bank has announced that customers will be able to send payments from Australia and New Zealand to many Pacific Islands cost-free until February 2021.

This progress is encouraging. But we need to continue to address costs barriers to digital remittances — making the PFIP’s work (a partnership between UNDP  and @UNCDF) to support financial inclusion more crucial than ever.

Read an interview with Bram Peters, the Program Manager of PFIP here: https://ab.co/3nBjcEu 

👉🏽Check out the new edition of our SIDS Bulletin here: https://lnkd.in/gCqwzcC

Agricultural expansion to achieve food security in Small #Island Developing States has the potential to negatively impact their environments, damaging biodiversity and vulnerable ecosystems. Right now, the world’s agriculture systems make up 10% of #carbon emissions.  

So, as we strive for reliable, nutritious food sources in #SIDS, we should also be exploring greener agriculture models. In our 23rd UNDP SIDS Bulletin, we featured the exciting potential of #smartfarming and #artificialntelligence technology to feed the hungry and preserve our environment through: 
1- #Data collection for improved farming efficiency 
2- Reinvented farming techniques (such as computer algorithms for detecting harvest times) 
3-Indoor farming 
4-Plant-based production 

#Digital transformation through #AI is a promising path forward to improve both agricultural productivity and sustainability in SIDS. 
You can read more here: https://bit.ly/3iL2b74

Spotlight on #DigitalTransformation: 
We are witnessing Small Island Developing States all over the world turn to digital solutions to encourage #inclusive pandemic recovery. Just this week, #guineabissau  announced the launch of an initiative to digitize healthcare processes with support from UNDP. This project will expand service reach, increase efficiency and encourage data collection. Check it out here: https://lnkd.in/gCcWK2t

In the 23rd edition of the #SIDS Bulletin, we highlighted the digital transformation agenda of #papuanewguinea, where they are increasing digital capacity, access and investment through the world’s first public-private Digital Foreign Direct Investment (#FDI) working group and new e-transaction legislation and services for easy online banking. Actions like these will better integrate island businesses into global and local markets, boosting socioeconomic recovery. 
Read all about it here: https://lnkd.in/gQAjwak
